newsitem.title: CANADA: Eight confirmed dead in plane crash in Eastern Canada.
newsitem.headline: Eight confirmed dead in plane crash in Eastern Canada.

text.p: Eight people aboard a twin-engine plane were killed when it crashed into a field in eastern Canada while attempting an emergency landing on Sunday, police said.

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said the Piper Nahavo from Waterville, Maine, was on its way to Bangor, Maine, from Anticosti Island in Quebec when it radioed the airport in Charlo, New Brunswick, and reported mechanical problems.

The plane was a few miles (km) from Charlo airport when it went down about noon (11 a.m. EDT) (1500 GMT) near the village of Eel River Crossing. Police said they were called to the scene of the crash shortly afterward but found no survivors.
Police said the plane was owned by Telford Aviation in Waterville, Maine, but the names and nationalities of the victims were not yet known. No further details were available.
